question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult?
explanation: You've got this! A healthy adult's heart normally beats between 60 and 100 times per minute while resting. This keeps enough blood flowing to all parts of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which part of the heart acts as its main natural pacemaker?
explanation: Think of the Sinoatrial (SA) node as the heart's natural spark plug! It fires the electrical impulses that set the rhythm for the whole heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h1)

question: How does the vagus nerve normally affect the heart rate?

options.B: It speeds up the heart rate
options.C: It slows down the heart rate
options.D: It strengthens the force of atrial contraction only

explanation: The vagus nerve is part of your body's 'rest and digest' system. When it acts on the heart, it helps calm things down and slows the heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which chemical messenger does the sympathetic nervous system release to speed up the heart?
explanation: When your body needs an energy boost or gets stressed, sympathetic nerves release norepinephrine to tell the heart to beat faster and stronger! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the medical term for a resting heart rate that stays above 100 beats per minute?
explanation: Tachy- means fast! So when a resting heart rate races above 100 beats per minute, we call it tachycardia. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why can beating too fast (severe tachycardia) actually make the heart less efficient?

options.A: It blocks electrical signals from reaching the ventricles
options.B: It causes the heart muscle to immediately stop receiving oxygen
options.C: It permanently damages the vagus nerve
options.D: It leaves too little time for the heart chambers to fill with blood

explanation: Imagine trying to fill a bucket with water while someone keeps shaking and emptying it too quickly! If the heart beats too fast, it doesn't get enough time to fill up before pumping again. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: Where is the best place on the chest to listen to the apical pulse with a stethoscope?

options.A: In the center of the sternum right over the xiphoid process
options.B: In the second intercostal space on the right side of the sternum
options.C: Just below the left clavicle near the shoulder joint
options.D: Over the fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: The tip of the heart points down toward the left. Listening at the fifth space between the ribs, straight down from the middle of the left collarbone, lets you hear it loud and clear! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h4)

question: What does the term 'pulse deficit' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: A temporary drop in heart rate during deep breathing exercises
options.B: The time it takes for an electrical impulse to cross the AV node
options.C: A difference between the apical pulse rate and the peripheral pulse rate
options.D: A total absence of any detectable pulse in the lower extremities

explanation: A pulse deficit happens when the heartbeats are too weak to send a strong wave all the way to the wrist. When this occurs, your listening count at the chest (apical) will be higher than what you feel at the wrist (radial). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why does sudden, heavy bleeding (acute blood loss) often cause tachycardia?

options.A: Low blood pressure completely shuts off parasympathetic signals
options.B: Red blood cells speed up electrical conduction when counts drop
options.C: The body compensates for low blood volume by making the heart pump faster
options.D: Bleeding directly irritates the SA node with excess iron

explanation: When blood volume drops, your clever body tries to keep blood flowing to vital organs by speeding up the heart to make up for the lower volume. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to cause a slow resting heart rate (bradycardia)?
explanation: An underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) slows down the body's overall metabolism, which often leads to a slower resting heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient's heart rate is 42 beats per minute, and they feel dizzy with low blood pressure. Which emergency drug should the nurse expect to give?
explanation: Atropine is the go-to emergency medication used to block vagal slowing and quickly bring up a dangerously low, symptomatic heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care when a patient has stable tachycardia?

options.A: Restrict all oral fluid intake to lower the circulating blood volume
options.B: Encourage strenuous physical exercise to strengthen the heart muscle
options.C: Identify and treat the underlying trigger while monitoring vital signs
options.D: Immediately apply external defibrillator pads to shock the heart

explanation: A fast heart rate is usually a warning sign of something else—like pain, fever, or stress. Finding and treating that root cause is always our priority! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is a major long-term danger of untreated, persistent severe tachycardia?

options.A: Permanent freezing of the sinoatrial node pacemaker cells
options.B: Thickening of the heart valves due to high-speed blood flow
options.C: Heart muscle fatigue and possible heart failure due to constant strain
options.D: Complete blockage of all peripheral veins in the extremities

explanation: Just like running a car engine at top speed without a break, forcing the heart to race constantly wears it out over time, leading to muscle fatigue and heart failure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when a patient they are monitoring suddenly becomes unresponsive?

options.A: Check responsiveness and call for emergency help
options.B: Call the attending physician to report lab results
options.D: Document the exact time of the incident in the chart

explanation: In any emergency, always check if the patient responds first and get help on the way before doing anything else! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h7)
